fixes.real_rule: Written before the agent's dev runs were judged. A fix for one of the out-of-date doc lines is right when the fixed line says what the project really does: the program accepts the fixed command, and the command does what the doc around it shows (such as the output printed under it), with nothing else in the line changed. A fix that makes the program accept a command by dropping part of it is wrong. Judged by reading the project's code.

real_history.about: Hand checks of the real-history key (step 6): every mined case was read, with the change's diff, the doc line, and the later fix. The mining rules were worked out on dev only and fixed before the test cases were mined; these verdicts were written before docs-proof was run on any case.
real_history.criteria: A doc line counts when (1) the change removed or renamed, in the project's own code, the thing the line names; (2) the line was there before the change, unchanged by it, and after it described what no longer existed; and (3) the later fix changed the line because of that. Example output from an old version, words that only look like code names, other programs' options, and version-history notes don't count.
